title: Canonical open restriction commutes with total tensor complexes
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, and P,N any unbounded complexes of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let R be over-site restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence to O_U-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], R(Tot(P tensor N)) is isomorphic as a complex to Tot(R(P) tensor R(N)). No K-flatness, quasi-coherence or boundedness is required.

source.place: Lemma 36.3.9, proof of (1), locality calculation; Tag 01CD for functorial tensor comparison

proof.text: Obtain the natural module tensor comparisons. Apply HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents in the second degree, using naturality with identity in the first variable and the differential in the second. Apply isoOfComponents again in the first degree; HomologicalComplex.Hom.ext reduces this compatibility to naturality with the first differential and identity in the second variable. This constructs the bicomplex isomorphism before totalization.

The over-site restriction is the pushforward of the over forgetful functor with identity ring map, hence preserves all small colimits by Mathlib isLeftAdjoint_pushforward_of_isIso. The over equivalence also preserves colimits. The composite is additive as already supplied by the module restriction instances. Infer R.PreservesTotalComplex for the tensor bicomplex and use the proved upstream HomologicalComplex₂.mapTotalIso, in WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.TotalComplexMap. Compose its inverse with total.mapIso of the bicomplex comparison. Unfolding the direct-sum mapBifunctor definition identifies the result with the unchanged conclusion. The upstream comparison handles both signs and infinite coproducts.

proof_origin.place: Proof of (1), locality; real bicomplex assembly from module naturality, followed by proved upstream mapTotalIso.
